Use this step‑by‑step checklist to evaluate any unexpected lottery notification:

import re
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser

# Load an email from a file (raw RFC 822 format)
with open('sample_email.eml', 'rb') as f:
    msg = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parse(f)

subject = msg['subject'] or ''
from_addr = msg['from'] or ''
body = msg.get_body(preferencelist=('plain', 'html'))
text = body.get_content() if body else ''

flags = []

# Simple checks
suspicious_keywords = [
    r'\b(pay|fee|tax|processing charge|transfer|wire|gift card|prepaid card|bitcoin|crypto)\b',
    r'\b(immediately|urgent|act now|confidential|secret|do not tell)\b',
    r'\b(winner|congratulations|you have won|prize|lottery|sweepstake)\b',
    r'\b(bank account|routing number|ssn|social security|passport|id number)\b'
]

for pattern in suspicious_keywords:
    if re.search(pattern, (subject + ' ' + text).lower()):
        flags.append(f'Keyword match: {pattern}')

# Check sender domain suspiciousness
m = re.search(r'@([^\s>]+)', from_addr)
if m:
    domain = m.group(1).lower()
    # simple heuristics: look for free email providers or very long domains
    free_providers = ('gmail.com', 'yahoo.com', 'hotmail.com', 'outlook.com')
    if domain in free_providers:
        flags.append('Sender uses a free email provider (possible impersonation)')
    if len(domain) > 30 or domain.count('-') > 2:
        flags.append('Suspicious-looking sender domain')

# Output results
if flags:
    print('Potential scam indicators found:')
    for f in flags:
        print(' -', f)
else:
    print('No obvious scam indicators detected. Still verify independently.')
